LESSON: SEASONS IN THE COUNTY - HOT, - COLD, - DRY - RAINY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Built Environments
Topic 1.4: Seasons in the County - Hot, - cold, - dry - rainy
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Seasons in the County - Hot, - cold, - dry - rainy, part of Natural and Built Environments in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How do seasons influence human activities in the county? 2. How important are the seasons in a county?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Seasons in the County - Hot, - cold, - dry - rainy together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learners develop relationships as they work collaboratively in groups discussing how different seasons affect

human activities in the county and sharing the discussion points in class.

● Digital Literacy: learners interact with technology as they use digital resources to identify seasons experienced in the county

(Hot, cold, dry, and rainy season).

Values:
• Respect: learners enhance the skill of acceptance as they appreciate diverse opinions as they brainstorm in groups about

seasons experienced in the County.

• Unity: learners enhance the skill of cooperation as they strive to achieve a common goal as they observe and record in charts

human activities associated with different seasons.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs) :

● Safety and security: learners will know to take safety precautions as they use print to digital resources to identify seasons

experienced in the county (Hot, cold, dry, and rainy seasons)

● Citizenship: learners engage effectively with others as they sing songs about seasons experienced in the County

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Creative Arts: learners sing and sign sing songs about seasons experienced in the County

• Science and Technology: learners find out from parents or guardians how to conserve the main physical features in the county

and share
